changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7997-detail-view-related-retired.md`

- names `RecordDetailView.tsx` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Why it retired.** `@objectstack/spec` declares no `DetailView` schema at all — every `DetailView` occurrence in `packages/spec/src` is prose about this repo's own `RecordDetailView.tsx` — so this array mirrored no protocol schema and drifted freely: it declared `columns` as `TableColumn[]` while the renderer it fed also accepted bare field names, `{ field, label }` and legacy `{ name, label }` spellings. The axis that carried the ruling was measured **zero pull**: no application code authored the member, both internal producers of a `detail-view` node (`RecordDetailDrawer`, `renderers/record-details.tsx`) synthesize it without `related`, and the only in-tree authorings carrying real columns were two documents — both rewritten here.

- names `renderers/record-details.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Why it retired.** `@objectstack/spec` declares no `DetailView` schema at all — every `DetailView` occurrence in `packages/spec/src` is prose about this repo's own `RecordDetailView.tsx` — so this array mirrored no protocol schema and drifted freely: it declared `columns` as `TableColumn[]` while the renderer it fed also accepted bare field names, `{ field, label }` and legacy `{ name, label }` spellings. The axis that carried the ruling was measured **zero pull**: no application code authored the member, both internal producers of a `detail-view` node (`RecordDetailDrawer`, `renderers/record-details.tsx`) synthesize it without `related`, and the only in-tree authorings carrying real columns were two documents — both rewritten here.

### `.changeset/8400-kanban-name-field-skip-set.md`

- names `record-details.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx` — edited by this change

  > Deliberately one rung, unlike the same dedupe in `record-details.tsx`, which also carries `deriveTitleField`: that ladder filters a synthesized field list, whereas this one filters an author-declared `cardFields`, where dropping a field the author asked for is a worse failure than a repeated title. A regression test pins both directions, including an object whose declared and derived pointers disagree.

### `.changeset/8649-detail-renderer-undeclared-keys.md`

- names `record-details.tsx` → `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-details.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **`@object-ui/plugin-detail` — the annotation-erasing destructure default is gone from three renderers.** `record-details.tsx`, `record-highlights.tsx` and `record-related-list.tsx` each annotated `schema` correctly and then wrote `schema = {} as any`. A destructuring default's type joins the annotated property type at the binding, so `any` erased the annotation for *every* read site in the file — declared keys and undeclared ones alike read `any`. No published surface moves: the exported annotations were always correct.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `b274b6103` (merge-base with origin/main): 7 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1406 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1985 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36096428207)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `664774d7a8aefcca25801ad170ded3178234af61`

Rendered by an isolated review subagent spawned by the `domain:ui#4` seat; its served tier was checked against its transcript stamps (117 of 117 model stamps at the review tier). Adopted by this seat.

### ① Derived judgments

- **(a) The gate at each host — the precedent's check, `id` and `_id` kept.** The helper returns the record untouched when `!perms?.isLoaded` (the frozen no-provider answer from `usePermissions()` has `isLoaded: false`, and `MePermissionsProvider` publishes `isLoaded: false` until its fetch settles), when `objectName` is empty, or when the record is not an object; otherwise it keeps a key when `key === 'id' || key === '_id' || perms.checkField(objectName, key, 'read')` and hands back the SAME object when nothing was withheld. That is objectui#10411's `!perms.isLoaded || perms.checkField(object, f, 'read')`; the precedent's extra `idField` exemption has no counterpart here because both floors (`resolveDisplayTitle` and `getRecordDisplayName`) read `id ?? _id` only.
  - `DetailView.tsx`: `titleRow` is a `React.useMemo` whose body is `withoutDeniedFields(data, perms, rawSchema.objectName)` and whose deps are `[data, perms, rawSchema.objectName]`; it is read once, in the H1 call `resolveDisplayTitle(titleRow, schema, objectSchema, ...)`. `perms` is in the deps. Nothing else moved: the summary chips, actions, sections, `$expand` and every `data?.[field]` read still take the raw `data` or `gatedSchema` as before.
  - `record-details.tsx`: `const data: any = withoutDeniedFields(ctx.data ?? {}, perms, objectName)`, computed in render after the two early returns (the `!ctx` placeholder and the capability gate), with `usePermissions()` called above them, so the hook order is unchanged and `perms` is read every render. `data` is read only by the dedupe ladder (the declared-pointer test, `formatTitleTemplate`, the candidate scan, the rendered-field scan). The `DetailView` node is synthesized from `ctx.data` raw, so the body's field values are untouched.
  - `RecordDetailView.tsx`: the title effect calls `getRecordDisplayName(objectDef, withoutDeniedFields(pageRecord, perms, objectName))` with deps `[pageRecord, objectDef, recordTitle, perms, objectName]`. `pageRecord` itself, the action handlers, the row predicates and the `data={pageRecord}` props are untouched.
  - A2 holds: with no provider, or before the policy loads, the helper returns the same object, so every title is byte-identical to base. Pinned by both no-provider controls.
  - A1 holds on every rung: `formatTitleTemplate` resolves a token by walking `record[p]`, so an absent key and a removed key both reach `undefined` and become the empty token; the orphan-separator class is hyphen, en dash, em dash, `|`, `/`, `·`, `,`, `:` — parentheses are not in it, so `{name} ({email})` renders `Ada Lovelace ()` for a removed key exactly as for a stripped one. `recordDisplayValueAt` reads `record[field]` and answers `undefined` for both. `getRecordDisplayName`'s record-key probe walks `Object.keys(record)`, so a removed key is not walked, exactly as a stripped key is not.
- **(b) The helper.** `packages/plugin-detail/src/withoutDeniedFields.ts` is not exported from `packages/plugin-detail/src/index.tsx`, the vite entry that `dist/index.*` is built from; a grep of the entry for the symbol is empty. The `RecordDetailView.tsx` copy is a non-exported `function`. The two bodies are identical line for line; the only textual difference is the parameter type spelled through the local alias `FieldReadPolicy` in one and inline as the same Pick over `usePermissions`'s return in the other. Behaviourally identical. Drift note, not a blocker: these are the third and fourth spellings of the rule in the tree (`LookupField.tsx` and `RecordPickerDialog.tsx` carry two more, with `idField`); each copy's doc comment names the others, which is the only thing holding them together, and nothing re-derives their agreement. A shared home would widen some package's published surface, which is what the PR declines.
- **(c) A3, the dedupe.** With the block's own header (`showHeader: true`) the H1 is DetailView's `titleRow` H1 and the dedupe runs the same function over the same `ctx.data`, so the row hidden is the row the H1 shows; reading the raw row hid the denied field's row (already hidden by `gatedSchema`) and left `name` printed directly under an H1 `Ada Lovelace`, which is what the WITH ITS OWN HEADER pins red on. Under `page:header` (the synthesized default page: `buildDefaultDetails` emits `record:details` with explicit `sections` and no `showHeader`, so the block draws no header of its own) `PageHeaderRenderer` reads `ctx.data` raw with no permission read, so on a backend that serves what the policy denies the H1 prints the denied value while the dedupe now hides the fallen-through `name` row. The dev's table re-derives from the ladder: `{email}` → gated template empty → candidate walk hides `name`; `{name} - {email}` → gated template collapses to `Ada Lovelace` → matches `name`; `nameField: 'email'` → pointer absent, template absent → candidate walk hides `name`.
  - No denied value is shown by this PR's change on any path: DetailView draws only `schema.sections` and `schema.fields`, both filtered by `gatedSchema`'s `checkField`, and `buildDefaultDetails` always passes explicit `sections`; the dedupe can only hide, never draw; the `page:header` H1 leak predates the PR.
  - Ruling on the seat's answer A: sound. Quantified: relative to base, A changes user-visible output on exactly one path — a backend that serves what the loaded policy denies, AND a policy that denies the very field the title reads, AND the `page:header` composition — and there it hides one body row (the fallen-through `name`) beneath an H1 that already prints the denied value; for a single-field title the readable name is then on screen nowhere, for a composite it is still in the H1. B would avoid that row loss but, on the same backend and policy, print the fallen-through name twice on the `showHeader: true` composition and would have to be re-gated when `page:header` is gated; C encodes the interim. On ObjectStack (`FieldMasker` runs `delete result[field]` on every unreadable key) A and B are both byte-identical to base in both compositions. A is the end state; its one interim cost lands on the path the dev's finding 1 already owns, so the seat should record it on that sub-card so the sub-card's pin covers the `name` row returning.
- **(d) The pins are real and can fail.** All three files mount the real `PermissionProvider` from `@object-ui/permissions` with a `viewer` role and `fieldPermissions` `read: false` per denied field; no stub. Counts from the case lists: DetailView 3 + 4 templates + 1 id floor = 8 denied pins, 2 controls, 10; record-details 3 WITH ITS OWN HEADER + 5 DENIED READS AS ABSENT (three header off, two header on) = 8 denied pins, 2 controls, 10; RecordDetailView 2 denied, 2 controls, 4; 24 in all. The reverse proofs re-derive from those lists: removing the DetailView gate reds its 8 plus the 5 record-details pins that read DetailView's H1 (3 WITH ITS OWN HEADER + 2 DENIED READS AS ABSENT with the header on) = 13, leaving 2 + 3 + 2 + 4 = 11 green; removing the record-details gate reds exactly its 8 (on the raw row `{email}` hides `email` instead of `name`, and `{email} - {phone}` hides nothing instead of `phone`, so the header-off equality pins differ too); removing the RecordDetailView gate reds its 2; removing the `id` exemption reds only the id-floor pin, since no other pin denies `id`. Consistent. No vacuous pin: every equality pin also asserts the denied value is absent, and the RecordDetailView pins record every published title so a transient publish would fail them. One limit: the pin provider is synchronous, so the window before an async policy loads is not exercised (see ③). The ablation runs themselves are the dev's readings and were not re-run here.
- **(e) Changeset truth.** `.changeset/10434-record-title-fls.md`: every sentence checked against head — `gatedSchema` hides denied rows while the header read `data`; the record page title feeds the breadcrumb, `addRecentItem` and `refreshFavoriteLabel`; `id` and `_id` are kept so the Record-number floor still applies; denied reads as absent per (a); no placeholder; `record:details` hides at most one row (`find` / `break`) and now chooses it from the same row; the `page:header` caveat matches (c); before load and with no provider nothing is removed; `FieldMasker` deletes denied keys (`delete result[field]` in objectstack's `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/field-masker.ts`). No line-address citation. `.changeset/9436-detail-declared-pointer-order.md`: front matter (`'@object-ui/plugin-detail': minor`) byte-identical — sha256 `4f730b5dced4eeafcc8e0fc78a1ebfa88a07476422e71afc4b14dbe396bd9791` at both the merge-base and head, computed here. The corrected sentences are true at head: a denied `primaryField` or pointer is absent from `titleRow`, so `resolveDisplayTitle` falls through as if blank; the dedupe's pointer branch runs `recordDisplayValueAt` on the gated row. The correction was forced: without it the pending body would say the dedupe hides the pointer's row "when it holds a value", which the gated row falsifies for a denied pointer on a non-stripping backend. The claims-gate hits re-read: 7997 (both `detail-view` producers synthesize without `related` — still true, the node synthesized here has none), 8400 (`record-details.tsx`'s dedupe "also carries `deriveTitleField`" — still true), 8649 (`record-details.tsx` no longer destructures `schema = {} as any`; `enforceFieldSecurity`, `redactFields` and `requiredPermissions` honoured unchanged — still true, `filterList` and the capability gate are untouched). Of the other pending changesets naming `resolveDisplayTitle`, `titleFormat`, `getRecordDisplayName`, `gatedSchema` or `RecordDetailView` (the head grep lists 57), the ones describing these hosts' title behaviour — 8175, 8350, 8351, 10360 and the two 9436 bodies — describe which row hides or which rung wins and remain true, because the gated row only removes keys a stripping backend would not serve; none asserts the raw row is read.
